scores.label: Scoped WSG audit score
scores.formula: 100 * passed / (passed + failed + cantTell), grouped once per guideline

impactWeighted.status: Experimental project convention using WSG impact priority points; not a W3C site score

scores.interpretation: Passes satisfy only the declared scoped expectations; unknowns earn no points but are not defects. Compare only matching rubric, sample, and evidence profiles.

guidelines.title: Identify, assess, disclose, review, and mitigate sustainability impacts
guidelines.expectation: A retrieved public sustainability statement identifies the audited service and describes its impacts and mitigation. Judge disclosure only, not execution; an unresolved relationship is cantTell.

judgments.rationale: The mission statement discusses broad web impacts, WSG development, implementation measurement and outreach. It does not identify www.w3.org operational impacts and mitigation. It is genuine mission context but cannot establish the narrow audited-service disclosure, nor does bounded absence prove such a statement does not exist.
judgments.nextEvidence: Supply a service-specific statement for the public W3C website operation/delivery if available.

guidelines.title: Understand user requirements or constraints
Integrate sustainability into every stage of the ideation process
Design efficient and streamlined user journeys
guidelines.expectation: Execute declared task actions and inspect completion evidence; an expected selector is one observable, not proof of user success or optimal journey length.

judgments.rationale: The declared route follows standards to the catalogue, enters WCAG, activates Show results and opens the exact WCAG 2.2 URL with its full visible title. The after state contains the full report body, and the independent task trace corroborates it. This supports desktop pointer completion without asserting shortest route or all-user usability.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

guidelines.title: Design to assist and not to distract
guidelines.expectation: Assess visible distractions against the declared visitor task; distinguish useful prompts from interruptions.

judgments.rationale: The seven samples present task headings, indexes, side navigation and relevant status information. No autoplay media or disruptive visible modal is recorded; WCAG permalink dialogs remain hidden. Catalogue result counts assist filtering and mission sponsorship links are recognizable. This is limited to the sampled states, not every interaction.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

guidelines.title: Avoid being manipulative or deceptive
guidelines.expectation: Inspect choice wording, defaults, prominence and the observed accept/reject paths for undue steering. DOM text alone does not establish visual parity.

judgments.rationale: No cookie banner or accept/reject pair is observed in the seven fresh page states; the walkthrough records that limit explicitly. Reading and catalogue filtering require no account, while membership/sign-in routes are identifiable. Defaults, visual choice prominence and any applicable consent route are not sufficiently tested to establish the whole choice expectation or a deceptive defect.
judgments.nextEvidence: If judging consent/choice parity, capture the applicable controls and defaults in the represented context; do not infer tracking absence from no banner.

guidelines.title: Make deliverables understandable and reusable
guidelines.expectation: Assess the sampled task's wording, headings and terminology for its stated audience; retain uncertainty about unrepresented users.

judgments.rationale: Headings and introductory summaries distinguish standards, normative WCAG requirements and beginner WAI resources. Catalogue examples, report status/version links and contact categories explain the tasks in context. Specialist WCAG terms suit the normative-document audience and introductory alternatives are supplied. This does not prove comprehension by unrepresented readers.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

guidelines.title: Use a design system for interface consistency
guidelines.expectation: Compare repeated navigation and control names across sampled pages; consistent samples do not prove a documented design system.

judgments.rationale: Corporate pages repeat the same named navigation and catalogue controls. WAI pages share their own consistent resource navigation, while the normative report uses a document-specific table of contents and version metadata. These recognizable template differences serve distinct tasks and are not inconsistent control naming; no maintained design system is inferred.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

guidelines.title: Optimize media to reduce resource use
guidelines.expectation: The sampled task images preserve useful content and provide proportionate intrinsic dimensions and delivery choices for their rendered size and pixel density. A large image is an investigation candidate until legibility and task value are checked; absent srcset alone is not a failure.

judgments.rationale: Most task content is text with modest logos/icons and selected homepage images. Responsive 640-pixel cards and 250-pixel member logos have plausible rendered sizes; a WAI 1833-pixel graphic displayed around 832 is compatible with higher density. Some SVG intrinsic-size comparisons are not raster waste. No visual quality/rendition inspection supports specific reductions or full proportionality across the sample.
judgments.nextEvidence: Inspect representative raster graphics at intended densities and task detail before reducing dimensions.

guidelines.title: Ensure animation is proportionate and easy to control
guidelines.expectation: Assess observed animation purpose, playback controls and reduced-motion behavior. A quiet snapshot does not prove no motion occurs elsewhere.

judgments.rationale: No screen animations or moving media are observed in desktop, narrow, reduced-motion and dark states. Two one-iteration link animations appear on each WAI print transition, without effect properties or visible purpose. This is insufficient to judge every recorded motion as proportionate or controlled, and does not demonstrate harmful animation.
judgments.nextEvidence: Inspect the WAI link-transition effects during print/preference changes; assess visible purpose and reduced-motion response.

guidelines.title: Use optimized web typography
guidelines.expectation: Observed web fonts and variants serve the sampled content, with a declared fallback/loading strategy where needed. Do not fail a site merely for using a web font; recommend removal or subsetting only after language and readability requirements are established.

judgments.rationale: Corporate and WAI content use loaded Noto Sans regular/semibold with fallback display and system fallback families; WAI code examples can use Noto Sans Mono. WCAG uses system sans-serif and downloads no webfont in the observation. Unloaded Arabic/icon declarations are not evidence of transfer. This meets the bounded observed strategy without assuming removable language support.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

guidelines.title: Avoid unwanted notifications
guidelines.expectation: Assess observed alerts and notification permission requests for user value and choice; absence is limited to observed states.

judgments.rationale: No Notification permission calls occur on the seven samples. Catalogue live result counts and empty status nodes support task feedback, while WCAG dialogs are hidden. With notification permission already denied, the pass is bounded to observed states rather than all messaging behavior.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

guidelines.title: Reduce the impact of downloadable and physical documents
guidelines.expectation: Review print layout visibility and download labels for the declared task. Fetch and inspect document content before asserting optimization or equivalence.

judgments.rationale: The sampled content is directly readable HTML and no document download links are listed. Print emulation retains content and suppresses much navigation. However catalogue print text expands from about 46,687 to 177,697 characters; whether that prints useful historical entries or unnecessary pages is unresolved without pagination inspection. No paper-saving or optimized-document equivalence claim is made.
judgments.nextEvidence: Inspect catalogue print pagination and hidden/expanded report details, retaining necessary version/status context.

guidelines.title: Involve users early in the project
Audit and test for bugs or issues requiring resolution
Validate usability through testing and real-world usage
Provide cross-platform compatibility support
guidelines.expectation: The sampled core reading content and navigation remain available without JavaScript, or an explicit alternative supports the task. This bounded check does not establish no-JavaScript search, every interaction, or all browser compatibility.

judgments.rationale: Fresh no-JavaScript states preserve the catalogue list/filter markup, complete WCAG text, WAI summaries/navigation and corporate mission/contact reading. No account or script-dependent player is required for the declared reading tasks. This supports the HTML baseline without claiming every search/menu interaction works without scripts.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

guidelines.title: Set goals based on performance and energy impact
Minify and remove unused code
guidelines.expectation: Use initial JS/CSS execution observations to nominate investigation targets; require representative journeys or source corroboration before recommending removal.

judgments.rationale: The report and WAI templates have small distinct enhancement scripts; corporate/catalogue templates load shared and page modules. Initial 500 ms coverage cannot establish safe removal across menus, filters, translations and report navigation. Unexecuted offsets are investigation candidates only.
judgments.nextEvidence: Capture representative interactions or source corroboration before identifying any removable module.

guidelines.title: Modularize bandwidth-heavy components
guidelines.expectation: Relate initial script resources to visible components and later task needs; recommend splitting only when a component's deferred use and usable activation are corroborated.

judgments.rationale: Corporate, catalogue, WAI and report scripts already differ by template. The sustainability page loads an embedded external video environment and has a partial 1,350,347-byte initial staged count, while its main reading content is immediately useful. No tested facade or usable activation comparison establishes safe further splitting or deferral.
judgments.nextEvidence: Compare initial embed with a user-activated video facade and verify playback, captions and accessible activation before recommending it.

guidelines.title: Avoid redundancy and duplication in code
Treat third parties the same as first parties
Ensure code follows good semantic practices
guidelines.expectation: The sampled document has a meaningful language, primary heading and main region, and task controls have visible labels or an explicit naming relationship. Count/attribute presence alone does not establish semantic correctness or WCAG compliance. The sampled initial keyboard path reaches visible task navigation/controls in a meaningful order with a discernible focus indicator. A bounded Tab trace cannot establish complete keyboard support, reverse navigation, traps or screen-reader accessibility.

judgments.rationale: The full WCAG report has meaningful en language and H1, but the recorded semantics find zero main elements or role=main regions, unlike the six other documents. This contradicts the selected main-region expectation for the full page sample. WAI Search inputs are named; the empty submit-button record needs a resolved accessible name before any separate naming defect. This is not a full WCAG assessment.
judgments.nextEvidence: Provide a main landmark around the normative report content while preserving its table-of-contents navigation, and verify landmark traversal.

judgments.rationale: Initial paths reach meaningful skip, language, navigation and report contents links. WAI focus outlines are solid blue and WCAG uses visible native outlines. Corporate skip/language controls have transparent outlines with no background/border/shadow comparison captured, so the full-sample discernible-indicator expectation remains unresolved rather than failed.
judgments.nextEvidence: Capture the corporate focused controls and their complete focus styling to confirm an indicator; retain the supported WAI/report behavior.

guidelines.title: Defer the loading of non-critical resources
Structure metadata for machine readability
guidelines.expectation: The sampled content has a descriptive title and usable canonical metadata when applicable; declared structured-data blocks parse as JSON. Judge description and other optional metadata according to page purpose, not a mandatory-field checklist.

judgments.rationale: Titles are descriptive and WAI/WCAG canonicals are usable; declared WAI JSON-LD parses. Corporate home, catalogue, mission and contact pages omit canonical metadata. Missing optional metadata is not automatically a defect, but catalogue query/filter variants make canonical applicability and the intended representative URL unresolved.
judgments.nextEvidence: Clarify the canonical/indexing policy for catalogue filter URLs and confirm when canonical metadata is applicable.

guidelines.title: Use media queries that support sustainability goals
guidelines.expectation: The sampled page respects applicable dark/reduced-motion preferences both before navigation and when they change in-page, without losing task content. Distinguish intentional design choices and absence of applicable motion from unsupported behavior.

judgments.rationale: All seven pages preserve task content during live/cold preferences. Their persistent light colors alone do not establish an applicable theme failure; WAI offers a Change Text Size or Colors route. Screen snapshots have no motion, but WAI print transitions record two running link animations without effect information. Full applicable preference behavior remains unresolved.
judgments.nextEvidence: Inspect the recorded link effects under reduced motion and exercise any documented preference controls before prescribing theme changes.

guidelines.title: Ensure layouts work for different devices and requirements
guidelines.expectation: Compare narrow and desktop task content and overflow, then exercise affected controls; width emulation alone is not real-device compatibility.

judgments.rationale: All seven desktop/narrow samples retain task headings and avoid measured horizontal overflow. Narrow corporate/WAI menus and the WCAG table of contents differ from desktop, but their affected controls were not activated in narrow state. Emulated width alone cannot establish complete task operation.
judgments.nextEvidence: Use the narrow menus and report navigation to complete the relevant information tasks.

guidelines.title: Use sustainable JavaScript and APIs
guidelines.expectation: Repeated observed API requests are justified by the sampled task and its update needs. Identify redundant-looking requests for investigation without inferring backend cost or safe removal from URL repetition alone.

judgments.rationale: The small corporate member-logo lookup and catalogue requests have plausible task purposes; the mission page also loads external video requests. Bounded snapshots do not establish sustained polling, freshness requirements or redundant API traffic. Repeated service endpoints cannot alone establish removal or backend savings.
judgments.nextEvidence: Trace recurring member/catalogue/embed calls by initiator and event, checking unchanged repeats against actual task needs.

guidelines.title: Use dependencies sparingly and maintain them
Include expected and beneficial files
guidelines.expectation: The sampled service exposes a discoverable, parseable carbon.txt with usable declared relationships. Missing carbon.txt is a scoped absence, not proof of high emissions or failure of the entire guideline. Judge redirects, delegation, supported versions and schema findings explicitly.

judgments.rationale: Root and well-known carbon.txt return 404 and no usable header/DNS delegation or parseable document is established. This is the narrow discovery absence only, not a statement about emissions or the usefulness of W3C sustainability work.
judgments.nextEvidence: If useful, publish a valid carbon.txt with supported service/provider relationships.

guidelines.title: Use the most efficient solution for your service
Use the latest stable language version
Reduce the number and complexity of database queries
Use sustainable hosting
guidelines.expectation: Hosting claims identify provider, service and supporting evidence with a relationship to this origin. Self-declaration without independently corroborated operational scope remains cantTell for sustainable hosting; do not set SWDM green-hosting flags from this check.

judgments.rationale: The frozen evidence does not relate this origin to a named hosting service with independently corroborated operational sustainability evidence. W3C sustainability advocacy and standards work are not hosting evidence.
judgments.nextEvidence: Provide an origin-to-hosting relationship and independent operational evidence for that service; do not set a green-hosting model flag from mission text.

guidelines.title: Optimize caching and support offline access
guidelines.expectation: Reusable public scripts/styles/media expose an appropriate caching or validation policy in the sample. Distinguish dynamic/private responses and note that headers alone do not prove cache reuse or offline support.

judgments.rationale: Reusable assets expose validation or caching policies: corporate CSS/JS use ETag and Last-Modified, catalogue fingerprinted assets use long public lifetimes, and WAI/TR styles/scripts have bounded lifetimes with validators where applicable. Missing max-age alone is not failed when validation exists. This does not establish actual warm reuse or offline access.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

guidelines.title: Reduce data transfer with compression
guidelines.expectation: Material sampled text assets are delivered with compression where beneficial. Do not demand compression for already-compressed images, tiny bodies or error responses without context.

judgments.rationale: Successful material text documents, scripts and styles use gzip or Brotli in all seven bounded response sets. The mission video-related zero-length text response is not material text needing compression. Already-compressed graphics/fonts/media are outside this demand.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

guidelines.title: Setup necessary error pages and redirection links
Avoid maintaining unnecessary virtualized environments or containers
Use automation wisely
Define the frequency of data refreshes
Back up critical data at routine intervals
Assess the impact and requirements of data processing
Use Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) when beneficial
Ensure infrastructure fits project requirements
Store data according to the needs of your users
Have an ethical and sustainable product strategy
Assign a sustainability advocate
Inform, raise awareness, and train for sustainability
Communicate the environmental impact of user choices
guidelines.expectation: Identify consequential user choices in the sample and assess whether contextual impact information is useful and supported. Do not prescribe carbon labels on every control.

judgments.rationale: Reading HTML, printing the catalogue/report, and choosing an embedded mission video have different potential resource implications. The mission discusses web-wide impacts, not measured differences between these choices. No tested media alternative or print-output comparison establishes what contextual guidance would be useful and supported.
judgments.nextEvidence: Compare one meaningful media/print choice for task value and transfer/page count before adding impact guidance.

guidelines.title: Calculate the environmental impact
Define clear organizational sustainability goals and metrics
guidelines.expectation: Published goals for the audited web service define a measurable target or direction, relevant metric and boundary, and communicate dated progress against a comparable baseline. A corporate net-zero ambition or isolated low-carbon badge cannot establish service-specific goals and progress.

judgments.assessmentScope: Operation and delivery of the public www.w3.org web service as described by its sustainability mission page at the 2026-11-06 capture. Assess whether published direction, metrics, service boundary and dated comparable baseline/progress refer to this service. W3C advocacy for the wider web and development of WSG are context, not evidence of this service achieving operational targets.
judgments.rationale: The mission describes a sustainable web direction, developing guidance and measuring implementations. It does not supply an operational metric, boundary and comparable dated baseline/progress for www.w3.org. Standards advocacy cannot establish achievement of the website's own targets; missing evidence is an unknown.
judgments.nextEvidence: Provide any public service-operation target, measurement boundary and comparable baseline/progress, if established.

guidelines.title: Validate web sustainability efforts through external verification
Support mandatory disclosures and reporting
Create one or more impact business models
Follow a product management and maintenance strategy
Implement continuous improvement procedures
Document updates and evolutions
Evaluate if a digital product or service is necessary
guidelines.expectation: For the declared visitor task and represented access constraints, inspect material accessibility, technical, geographic or fairness barriers and verify the sampled route or alternative supports task completion while preserving necessary security and safety. Do not demand removal of justified authentication or infer all-user accessibility from one successful route.

judgments.assessmentScope: Anonymous English desktop readers with JavaScript enabled, a pointer and ordinary text input at 1365x900: start at https://www.w3.org/, follow standards to the public technical-report catalogue, filter for WCAG and open the full WCAG 2.2 report. Completion requires its exact URL and visible full report title, with no account or personal-data submission. Keyboard-only, mobile, impaired-network and geographic access are not represented.
judgments.rationale: The represented anonymous 1365 by 900 desktop pointer/text-input route reaches the exact WCAG 2.2 report and visible full title without account or personal data. The full after text and independent trace establish the declared completion. This does not imply keyboard, network, geography or representative-user success.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

guidelines.title: Provide a supplier standards of practice document
Share economic benefits
Share decision-making power with affected parties
Use Diversity, Equity, Justice, Inclusion (DEJI) practices
Promote responsible data practices
guidelines.expectation: For a declared content collection, evidence identifies a review/expiry schedule and demonstrates an applied archive, update or deletion decision, with a lightweight discoverable historical version where users still need it. A date label, old article or policy alone cannot establish an effective lifecycle or justify deletion.

judgments.assessmentScope: Public English WCAG 2.2 technical-report collection, from the first 2020 working draft through the December 2024 Recommendation and its currently published history as captured on 2026-11-06: review stated maintenance/review arrangements, an applied publication/update decision and discoverable historical reports. The broader WAI collection and organization-wide CMS practices are excluded; continuing reference value of historical standards is retained.
judgments.rationale: WCAG 2.2 has an actual staged publication history from 2020 drafts through the 2024 Recommendation, current/versioned/editor/history/errata links, named editors and a feedback route. These are useful applied publication and historical-access evidence. The captured status excerpt does not identify a review/expiry schedule; later-version intentions are not a maintenance cadence. Consequently the exact combined expectation remains incomplete, without treating old standards as waste.
judgments.nextEvidence: Capture the collection's maintenance/review arrangement or cadence and one applicable update decision; preserve dated reports for continuing normative reference value.

guidelines.title: Establish responsible practices around AI and emerging or disruptive technologies
Adopt responsible financial practices
Adopt organizational philanthropy practices
Plan for a digital product or service's care and end-of-life
Repair, reuse, refurbish, recycle or reduce e-waste
Define performance, environmental, and human budgets
Use and contribute to open source
Create a business continuity and disaster recovery plan
